# [CS003] Path Traversal (path-traversal)

A file path is built from untrusted data without confinement.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) |
| **OWASP** | A01:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Names such as ../../etc/passwd or absolute paths escape the intended directory; filepath.Join and filepath.Clean do not prevent that. Go 1.24 os.Root confines every operation, including symlink resolution, to one directory, which also closes the race between a check and the open. Access through os.Root is never reported.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
func download(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	http.ServeFile(w, r, filepath.Join("/srv/files", r.URL.Query().Get("name")))
}
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func download(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	root, err := os.OpenRoot("/srv/files")
	if err != nil {
		http.Error(w, "unavailable", http.StatusInternalServerError)
		return
	}
	defer root.Close()
	f, err := root.Open(r.URL.Query().Get("name"))
	if err != nil {
		http.NotFound(w, r)
		return
	}
	defer f.Close()
	_, _ = io.Copy(w, f)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [path-traversal]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    path-traversal: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore path-traversal -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** path-traversal
```
